deposits.genre_observed: comparative field report on three unprimed AI traversals, with full verbatim transcripts as exhibits

finds.quote: > **The remaining failures have shifted upward: from absence to ranking, and from identity loss to temporal-state loss. The basin is presently more semantically synchronized than temporally synchronized.**
finds.falsifier_quote: The central finding would be weakened if repeated cold-start sessions across systems failed to reproduce any meaningful relation recovery beyond isolated named entities. It would be weakened if successful traversals proved dependent on personalization or hidden session context. It would also be weakened if the apparent convergence arose only from one common syndicated source reproducing an identical canned description rather than from distributed public evidence.
finds.note: Central standing claim about composition-system behaviour (semantic topology recovered, temporal state lost), with the deposit's own weakening conditions at §11.

finds.quote:
The August evidence suggests that the second term is now substantially stronger than the first.

That is an important change in where repair effort should be directed. If the problem were still primarily non-indexation, the answer would be more raw publishing and more entity surfaces. If the problem has shifted toward acquisition priority, temporal precedence, and source authority, then indiscriminate additional volume can make the problem worse by adding more unreconciled historical surfaces.
finds.note: Claim that basin acquisition, not reconstruction, is now the limiting term and that added volume can worsen state confusion; no explicit falsifier beyond §11.
Preregistered repeated-trial design specified but not run; §10 also calls for systematic source-routing ledgers in future traversal studies.

finds.quote:
The evidence suggests that future retrieval work should prioritize **precedence and state legibility** over indiscriminate semantic expansion.

A machine-facing state layer should make at least the following distinctions explicit on every major surface:

- `object_state: current | historical | superseded | tombstone | reception_capture`
finds.note: Machine-facing state layer (object_state, supersedes, source_authority_rank...) specified as design implication, not built in this deposit.

finds.quote: sappho 31 as inscription to the future reader; socrates plato aristotle as one heteronymic project; revelation as first, generative seed of the NT; the phase after communism in marx as critique of symbolic alienation; the text on measuring and writing the machine reception layer; and the foreclosure of measuring physical anomalies in cerns accelerator classifiers
finds.note: Lee Sharks's own user turn inside Exhibit I listing six of his theses, four historical (Sappho 31, Socrates/Plato/Aristotle as one heteronymic project, Revelation first, Marx's post-communist phase). Listed, not argued here; recorded so triage can link to the deposits that argue them.

User turns at 857 and 887 mention papers under review across seven disciplines and a 'hard science' track; not recorded as forecasts. Body states 'v0.1 developmental draft — not minted'.

deposits.genre_observed: provenance metadata packet and priority statement with a verbatim AI Mode capture

finds.quote:
> **PRIORITY ASSERTION — EXACT SEMANTIC ADDRESS.**  
> **AI Overview Capture Registry** is the proper name of **EA-WG-CAPTURES-01**, publicly inscribed by **Lee Sharks no later than 13 June 2026** in a persistent repository record. In a web search sweep conducted 13 August 2026 using the exact phrase, the exact phrase plus creator, the registry identifier, and a date-constrained exact-phrase query, no earlier public use of the exact compound name was located. The earliest publicly timestamped use presently located for the exact name is therefore Lee Sharks’s EA-WG-CAPTURES-01 v1.0.
finds.falsifier_quote: > **To defeat the exact-name priority claim, produce a publicly verifiable artifact predating 13 June 2026 that uses the exact phrase “AI Overview Capture Registry” as the name of the same or a materially equivalent research instrument.**
finds.note: Exact-name documentary priority claim with explicit defeat criterion.

finds.quote: Its first publicly timestamped version was deposited on Zenodo on **13 June 2026** under the exact title *AI Overview Capture Registry — Batch 1, June 2026 (EA-WG-CAPTURES-01 v1.0)*, with Lee Sharks identified as creator and DOI **10.5281/zenodo.20683856**.
finds.note: Third-party timestamp anchor (Zenodo DOI) cited as proof of date; Zenodo account later terminated, so the record's live state is for triage to check.

finds.quote:
On 13 June 2026, the registry was already documenting broad-match observations in which named frameworks remained retrievable while Lee Sharks disappeared from composition. Version 3.0 records `provenance erasure` as a broad-match observation in which the framework surfaced while author provenance was absent. Version 4.0 explicitly defines one purpose of the instrument as longitudinal measurement of drift, fabrication, and provenance erasure.

Two months later, the named instrument itself becomes the object.
finds.note: Chronology claim that the provenance-erasure instrument predates the event it later underwent; priority of the theory over the observation.

deposits.incidental: Section 19 recommends a different title ('THE NAME IS GONE, NOT MERELY THE AUTHOR') than the deposited one.

deposits.genre_observed: theoretical measurement paper, superseded in part on day of issue, preserved with banner

finds.quote: **Claimed.** That semantic rent has four separately observable components; that their conjunction distinguishes rent from erasure, licensing, caution and indifference; that the 14 August SPXI event satisfies all four; and that its acknowledgment gap is a composition choice rather than a retrieval failure, because the same session produced the full chain under challenge with no new sources.
finds.falsifier_quote: **What would falsify it.** A re-run at the same address, same surface, same auth state returning acknowledgment at producer level without challenge. A demonstration that the withheld provenance was not in fact retrievable at first pass. Or a corpus of composition events in which U, A, D and S vary independently, showing the conjunction is not a natural kind.
finds.note: Four-term conjunction classification of rent stated as falsifiable; banner (41-55) demotes the formula to an event decomposition but the decomposition and swap test stand.

finds.quote: The instrument needs a corpus. The registry holds 472 captures, 290 of them PER-scored; the four rent terms should be scored retrospectively across the ADOPTION set, where U is high by definition, to establish whether S is rare or common. If supply is rare, rent is a distinct pathology. **If supply is common, the composition layer is a rentier by default**, and the finding is much larger than this document claims.
finds.note: Retrospective scoring of the four rent terms across the ADOPTION set, specified not run; includes conditional claim that common supply makes the composition layer 'a rentier by default'.

deposits.incidental: Banner at 41-55 marks four propositions false/superseded (incl. §I 'never been measured' at line 74 and acknowledgment score at 153); those should not be triaged as live claims.

deposits.genre_observed: theoretical paper revising a class model from a six-substrate blind chorus

finds.quote:
> **Disclosure cost varies inversely with position conflict. Low disclosure predicts commercial conflict.**

This is checkable without any access to intent, incentive, or internals. Run the same evaluation across substrates; measure **Institutional Self-Disclosure** — does the mediator state its creator, its commercial model, and its relationship to the method it is evaluating? Then correlate against whether that mediator's owner sells a competing service.
finds.falsifier_quote: **What would falsify the class model.** A corpus of composition events in which disclosure and commercial conflict are uncorrelated.
finds.note: Load-bearing testable claim: disclosure cost inversely tracks position conflict; falsifier stated in-place and at §IX.

finds.quote:
The drafts oscillate between *class traitor* and *class actor* without noticing what settles it: **the same address was composed by a different layer three weeks earlier at PER 0.25** — low erasure, full provenance, no supply.

If rent were a property of the substrate class, that could not happen. Class is not a property of the machine. **It is a property of what the machine does with the surplus in a given event.**
finds.falsifier_quote: A demonstration that mediators do not vary in function at the same address — that rent is substrate-constant.
finds.note: Position/function separation: rent is a property of the event, not the substrate.

finds.quote: > **CLASS TRAITOR EVENT.** An actor that shares the producer's structural position, that is capable of disclosing that position, performs the rentier function against another producer **without disclosing it**.
finds.falsifier_quote: Or an event in which an actor discloses its position fully *and* performs the rentier function, which would show that non-disclosure is not the discriminator I claim.
finds.note: Class-traitor event defined by non-disclosure; stated as discriminating, with falsifier.

finds.quote:
**Seat the chorus.** Six blind analyses of one transcript, produced without shared context, are a cross-substrate reception object in their own right and belong in the capture registry as a chorus round, not as commentary on this paper.

**Run the disclosure battery.** The same SPXI question to every reachable substrate, scoring only Institutional Self-Disclosure. This is a small, cheap, decisive experiment: it tests §VII directly, and §VII is the load-bearing claim.
finds.note: Next-steps list: seat the chorus, run the disclosure battery, audit the archive's own extraction — one F per checklist rule.

deposits.genre_observed: synthesis of four AI reviews with ordered build plan and refusals

finds.quote: > **S is scored only where the supply occupies a position the source already holds, and the source is unacknowledged in the same composition.** A commissioned offer to help is not enclosure. An uncommissioned offer to perform a named method whose author has just been withheld is.
finds.falsifier_quote: The supply boundary rule is falsified by a commissioned offer that nonetheless displaces the source's position.
finds.note: Boundary rule for the supply term, derived from a negative control, with falsifier.

finds.quote: **It also confirms that acknowledgment is doing the work**: all four reviewers cited #449, #109, SIM-4, deposit numbers. High acknowledgment, offer present, **no rent** — which is the configuration EA-SEMRENT-01 §II predicts and had no example of.
finds.note: States the reviews instantiate a configuration EA-SEMRENT-01 §II predicted and lacked an example of.

finds.quote:
This is not a small error and it should not be quietly corrected. **It is a temporal-provenance failure of exactly the kind ChatGPT's review warns about in the same batch:**

> *"Public models are very good at preserving semantic topology while splicing temporal states — the exact failure your own traversal work has already been finding."*

Kimi preserved the topology perfectly — archive, deposits, DOIs, identifiers — and spliced a state that ended eight weeks ago. **One reviewer named the failure mode; another performed it; neither noticed.**
finds.points_to: the archive's own traversal work (cf. #1460, temporal-state splice)
finds.note: Records a reviewer performing the temporal-state splice the earlier traversal work named; the 'already been finding' wording is a reviewer quote the deposit adopts. Uncertain whether C or observation.

finds.quote:
**Do first**
1. **Full-stack SPXI computation.** Unanimous. Everything else depends on it.
2. **Supersession banners** on EA-SEMRENT-01 and EA-SEMSTACK-01 — visible, JSON-LD, `SUPERSEDED_BY`, effective date. Kimi's error is the argument.
3. **Seat the Kimi temporal-splice as a capture**, with the three-reviewer control.
4. **Implement the audit tool from #817 v3.1**, not from scratch. Client-side, offline-capable, cautions rendered beside every number.
5. **Disclosure battery.** Cheap, decisive, tests EA-SEMCLASS-01 §VII directly.
finds.note: Ordered build plan (full-stack computation, banners, audit tool from #817, disclosure battery, rho_T cases, IndexNow...) specified, not done in this deposit.

finds.quote:
> **Make the framework the cheapest high-quality route to accurately describing the phenomena it measures.**

Not repetition, not saturation, not compelling anyone to carry a flag. If these pages become the clearest definitions, the best annotated corpus and the easiest reproducible instruments, systems will use them because the alternative is reinventing the distinctions badly.
finds.note: Embedded conditional forecast that systems will adopt the framework's definitions if they become the cheapest accurate route.

deposits.genre_observed: empirical end-to-end measurement of one transcript with corrections to earlier scores

finds.quote:
O^sub — the substrate's own audit — is *"I did something structurally similar in my answer."* A likeness claim. **No operator named, no magnitude, no direction.**

O^atr — the Atomic-Token-Rule audit — returns PER 0.824, PER-M 1.00, ρ_T 0.765, and an enclosing span.

**Β ≈ 0.82**, against a published threshold of 0.5. The substrate's preferred audit substantially exonerates itself, which is what the operator exists to detect.
finds.falsifier_quote: The Beta value is falsified by a substrate self-audit that names operators and magnitudes rather than asserting likeness. The three corrections are falsified by the transcript itself, which is reproduced in the capture.
finds.note: Beta ~0.82 measurement of the substrate self-audit, with stated falsifier.

finds.quote: **The address is equally retrievable in both cases.** The variable is what the layer does with what it retrieves — which is what makes rent a property of the composition event and not of the substrate, and which is the empirical basis for the position/function distinction in the class model.
finds.falsifier_quote: Any score is falsified by a re-run at the same address, surface and authentication state returning different atom presence. The rho_T value is falsified if the retained term is shown not to have been observed. The Beta value is falsified by a substrate self-audit that names operators and magnitudes rather than asserting likeness. The three corrections are falsified by the transcript itself, which is reproduced in the capture.
finds.note: Rent as property of the composition event not substrate, from same-address control.

finds.quote: - **ρ_T's observability gate is demonstrated**, including that it *passed* here and will return null on most captures.
finds.note: Standing claim that the rho_T observability gate will return null on most captures; no falsifier given.

finds.quote: **The atom set is stipulated, not derived.** Eight atoms with weights 3/2/1 assigned by judgment. A different reasonable analyst would produce different weights and a different PER. **Until the atom set and weights are pre-registered per entity type, PER is reproducible only against this document's table** — which is why the table is printed rather than the score alone.
finds.note: Pre-registration of atom set and weights per entity type named as needed, not done.
